definitions.explanation: Having an innocent, pure quality typically associated with young children; lacking worldliness or guile.

examples.japanese: あどけない⟦{笑顔|えがお}→笑顔：01884_egao⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦たち→たち：01551_tachi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{遊|あそ}んでいた→遊ぶ：00550_asobu⟧。
examples.english: Children with innocent smiles were playing.

examples.japanese: ⟦まだ→まだ：00603_mada⟧あどけない⟦{表情|ひょうじょう}→表情：03585_hyoujou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{残|のこ}っている→残る：01187_nokoru⟧。
examples.english: There's still an innocent expression remaining (on their face).

examples.japanese: あどけない⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{見|み}つめられた→見つめる：04571_mitsumeru⟧。
examples.english: I was gazed at with innocent eyes.

notes:
・あどけない → あどけなく (adverbial)
・あどけない → あどけなくない (negative)
・あどけない → あどけなかった (past)
・あどけない → あどけなさ (noun form)

USAGE:
Typically describes children or young people, or adults who have retained a childlike quality. Often used positively to describe a pure, unspoiled quality.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・あどけない⟦{笑顔|えがお}→笑顔：01884_egao⟧ (innocent smile)
・あどけない⟦{表情|ひょうじょう}→表情：03585_hyoujou⟧ (innocent expression)
・あどけない⟦{顔|かお}→顔：00558_kao⟧ (innocent face)
・あどけない⟦{寝顔|ねがお}→寝顔：29325_negao⟧ (innocent sleeping face)

NUANCE:
Carries a warm, affectionate tone. Unlike ⟦{無邪気|むじゃき}→無邪気：18237_mujaki⟧ (innocent/naive), あどけない specifically emphasizes the visual appearance of innocence — it describes how someone looks, not how they behave.

forms.label: Conditional たら
forms.negative: あどけなくなかったら
